description: Master CDN Edge caching, Dynamic Site Acceleration (DSA), BGP Anycast routing, Cache-Control headers, invalidation strategies, and Edge Workers (Cloudflare Workers / Lambda@Edge).

topics.title: CDN Architecture: Points of Presence (PoPs), Edge Caching & Anycast BGP
topics.definition: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a geographically distributed network of Edge proxy servers (Points of Presence / PoPs) that cache and deliver web content (images, videos, HTML, API responses) close to end users to minimize latency and offload origin server infrastructure.
topics.why_we_need_it: Speed of light in fiber optic cables takes ~70ms to travel from Tokyo to Virginia. A user in Tokyo requesting data from an origin in Virginia experiences high latency and TCP handshake delays. Serving from a Tokyo CDN Edge PoP delivers content in <5ms.
topics.real_world_analogy: A global chain of neighborhood grocery convenience stores: instead of every customer flying to the central factory in Switzerland to buy chocolate, the factory ships pallets to local neighborhood stores so customers buy chocolate in 2 minutes.
topics.how_it_works:
1. BGP Anycast Routing: Multiple CDN PoP servers across 100+ countries share the exact same public IP address. Internet routers automatically direct user packets to the topologically closest PoP.
2. Static Content Delivery: Images, CSS, JS, and video segments are cached with long TTLs. Cache Hits never touch origin servers.
3. Dynamic Site Acceleration (DSA): For non-cacheable dynamic requests, CDN maintains persistent, warmed TCP/TLS connection pools to the origin and uses route optimization across private backbone fibers to bypass congested public internet routes.
conceptual_breakdown: Origin Shield (Tiered Caching): An intermediate caching layer between Edge PoPs and Origin that consolidates cache misses, preventing origin thundering herds.
Cache-Control Directives: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for versioned static assets; `s-maxage` for CDN caches vs `max-age` for browser caches.
Stale-While-Revalidate: Serves stale cached content instantly to user while asynchronously fetching fresh content from origin in the background.

topics.failure_scenarios: Instant Global Cache Invalidation Storm: Running a global wildcard purge (`PURGE /*`) on an e-commerce CDN flushes millions of cached items, causing 100,000 QPS of subsequent user traffic to hit origin servers simultaneously, crashing the database. Mitigation: Use versioned URLs (`/app.v2.js`) and soft purging.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using CDN cache purging as the primary mechanism for static asset updates.
common_mistakes.correction: Use Content Hashing / Cache Busting in file names (`bundle.a8f2c.js`) with 1-year immutable cache headers.

interview_questions.question: How does BGP Anycast direct users to the nearest CDN Point of Presence (PoP)?
interview_questions.answer: With BGP Anycast, all CDN edge data centers advertise the exact same IP prefix into the global Internet routing table (BGP). Upstream ISP routers compute the shortest AS-Path and automatically route the user's TCP packets to the topologically nearest PoP data center.

topics.title: Edge Computing: Cloudflare Workers, Lambda@Edge & V8 Isolates
topics.definition: Edge Computing executes lightweight application code and serverless functions directly at CDN edge nodes across the globe, processing user requests within microseconds of their physical location.
topics.why_we_need_it: Executing authentication checks, geolocation redirects, A/B testing variations, and personalization at the origin adds unnecessary cross-continental latency. Edge computing evaluates logic right at the user's doorstep.
topics.real_world_analogy: A border customs officer stamping visas at the airport gate (Edge) instead of making passengers fly to the capital city just to get a stamp before entering.
topics.how_it_works:
1. V8 Isolates (Cloudflare Workers): Instead of spinning up heavy Docker containers or VMs (which take 500ms+ to boot), Edge Workers run inside lightweight Google V8 JavaScript Isolates with <5ms startup time and tiny memory footprints.
2. Edge Key-Value / D1 Databases: Globally distributed, eventually consistent edge key-value stores (Workers KV, Upstash) replicated to all PoPs.
3. Common Use Cases: Dynamic A/B testing, JWT validation, geo-fencing, header mutation, dynamic image resizing, and bot mitigation.
conceptual_breakdown: Zero Cold Starts: V8 Isolates start in under 5 milliseconds.
Sub-Request Limits: Edge workers have strict CPU execution time limits (e.g. 50ms) to maintain edge throughput.
Edge Rendering (SSR): Rendering HTML pages at the edge using frameworks like Next.js and Remix.
topics.failure_scenarios: Origin State Desynchronization at Edge: An edge worker writes to a locally replicated edge KV store that has a 60-second replication propagation delay, causing a user traveling between regions to read stale state. Mitigation: Route writes to centralized databases or use strong consistency options.

common_mistakes.mistake: Running long compute-heavy machine learning inference or heavy batch parsing inside edge workers.
common_mistakes.correction: Keep Edge Workers focused on lightweight routing, auth validation, and rapid caching transforms; delegate heavy computing to core cloud data centers.

interview_questions.question: Why are V8 Isolates superior to containerized micro-VMs for Edge Computing?
interview_questions.answer: V8 Isolates share a single running process memory space while enforcing strict security isolation, allowing thousands of tenant scripts to run on a single edge server with zero container startup overhead, sub-millisecond cold starts, and minimal RAM footprint per tenant.
